sense: two people together: a married couple, partners

terms.gloss: a spouse; in the plural, husband and wife
terms.grammar: noun, third declension; in the plural, conjugēs, a married couple
evidence: Catull. 61.225–226: at, bonī conjugēs, bene vīvite
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: in the plural for the married pair (Catull. 61, 66). See spouse.

terms.gloss: a pair: two who belong together
evidence: Cic. Amic. 15: vix tria aut quattuor nōminantur paria amīcōrum
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: a pair, a couple, of people or animals.

evidence: Apul. Met. 8 (Lewis & Short): novī marītī, a young couple
terms.comment: Lewis & Short mark this plural post-classical: the jurists and Apuleius.

phrases.latin: lūsimus satis. at, bonī conjugēs, bene vīvite
phrases.english: we have played enough. And you, good husband and wife, live happily

phrases.latin: ex omnibus saeculīs vix tria aut quattuor nōminantur paria amīcōrum
phrases.english: from all the ages hardly three or four pairs of friends are named

sources: Lewis & Short: conjunx · Lewis & Short: par · Lewis & Short: maritus
